english: Let $P(\alpha,\beta)$ be a point in the first quadrant on the hyperbola $9x^{2}-16y^{2}=144$. The tangent to the hyperbola at $P$ meets the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis at $A$ and $B$ respectively, and the normal to the hyperbola at $P$ meets the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis at $C$ and $D$ respectively. hindi: माना कि अतिपरवलय $9x^{2}-16y^{2}=144$ पर प्रथम चतुर्थांश में एक बिन्दु $P(\alpha,\beta)$ है। $P$ पर अतिपरवलय की स्पर्श रेखा $x$-अक्ष तथा $y$-अक्ष को क्रमशः $A$ तथा $B$ पर मिलती है, और $P$ पर अतिपरवलय का अभिलम्ब $x$-अक्ष तथा $y$-अक्ष को क्रमशः $C$ तथा $D$ पर मिलता है। माना $O$ मूल बिन्दु है, तथा $\Delta_{1}$ और $\Delta_{2}$ क्रमशः त्रिभुजों $OAB$ और $OCD$ के क्षेत्रफल हैं। यदि $625\Delta_{1}=144\Delta_{2}$ है, तो $\beta^{2}$ बराबर है
solution_full: The hyperbola is $\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}=1$, so $a=4$, $b=3$ and $a^{2}+b^{2}=25$. A point in the first quadrant is $P(4\sec\theta,3\tan\theta)$ with $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Tangent at $P$: $\dfrac{x\sec\theta}{4}-\dfrac{y\tan\theta}{3}=1$. Putting $y=0$ gives $x=4\cos\theta$, and putting $x=0$ gives $y=-3\cot\theta$. Hence $OA=4\cos\theta$, $OB=3\cot\theta$ and $\Delta_{1}=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot4\cos\theta\cdot3\cot\theta=\dfrac{6\cos^{2}\theta}{\sin\theta}$.

Normal at $P$: $\dfrac{a^{2}x}{x_{1}}+\dfrac{b^{2}y}{y_{1}}=a^{2}+b^{2}$, i.e. $4x\cos\theta+3y\cot\theta=25$. Putting $y=0$ gives $x=\dfrac{25}{4}\sec\theta$, and putting $x=0$ gives $y=\dfrac{25}{3}\tan\theta$.
Since $\cos\theta>0$ and $\sin\theta>0$, this gives $\cos^{2}\theta=\sin\theta$, i.e. $1-\sin^{2}\theta=\sin\theta$, so $\sin^{2}\theta+\sin\theta-1=0$.

The roots are $\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt{5}}{2}$; only $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$ lies in $(0,1)$. The left side $\cos^{4}\theta-\sin^{2}\theta$ is strictly decreasing on $\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, so $P$ is unique.
Option (D) is $\alpha^{2}=16\sec^{2}\theta=\dfrac{16}{\sin\theta}=8(\sqrt{5}+1)$, not $\beta^{2}$; option (A) uses the wrong root sign.
originality_note: New: the point is fixed by a ratio of the two intercept triangles cut off by the tangent and by the normal at the same point (way 5); the ratio reduces to cos^4 = sin^2, a golden-ratio equation in sin(theta). Closest known: intercepts of the tangent and normal of a hyperbola on the axes; area of the triangle cut off by a tangent. Different because: two intercept triangles are compared, and the trigonometric equation cos^2(theta) = sin(theta) decides the point.

concept_use.Parametric coordinates for Hyperbola: P is written as (4 sec(theta), 3 tan(theta)); the areas and beta^2 are computed in theta, and beta^2 = 9 tan^2(theta) = 9 sin(theta).
concept_use.Tangent and normal for Hyperbola: The tangent and the normal at P in parametric form give the intercepts A, B, C, D and hence the two triangle areas.

key_step: Intercepts of tangent and normal in theta give cos^4(theta) = sin^2(theta), i.e. cos^2(theta) = sin(theta), and beta^2 = 9 sin(theta).
justification: Two linked ideas: parametric tangent and normal intercepts, then a trigonometric equation that must be read as cos^2 = sin to finish quickly. More than a routine chain but options help; comparable to 2026-P2-Q13 (L3) on hyperbola elements and above 2025-P2-Q4 (L2).
